newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LSWR bullish as heat pushes power demand up.
newsitem.headline: Japan LSWR bullish as heat pushes power demand up.

text.p: An unexpected heatwave in Japan has boosted interest in low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), which is mainly used by electric power utilities to generate power, oil product traders said on Monday.
"Although I haven't seen extra LSWR orders emerging from power firms yet, this hot weather has certainly set a bullish tone for the market," one trader said.
Temperatures in Tokyo reached 37.7 degrees Celsius on Saturday, 11 degrees higher than the average temperature for that day over the past several years.
As a result, Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc's (TEPCO) power output totalled 954.7 million kilowatt hours (kWh), up 18 percent from the same day a week ago.
On Sunday, Tokyo temperatures peaked at 35.8 degrees C, up by 8.9 degrees from the average.
TEPCO said its LSWR consumption had increased due to the heatwave, but that it was unclear by how much it had expanded.
Spot LSWR cargo prices have risen due to growing expectations of extra requirements from Japan, as well as Indonesia's smaller-than-usual LSWR allocation for July-lifting, traders said.
Spot Indonesian cargoes were assessed at $1.10 to $1.50 per barrel over the Pertamina formula, compared to premiums of about 50 to 70 cents a month ago.

Some traders, however, say additional orders from utilities are unlikely unless the hot weather continues for at least one Japan's Meteorological Agency said on Monday the heatwave had lost momentum, and that temperatures were expected to come down to normal levels towards the weekend.
In Japan, the operation of oil-fired power plants, which act as a buffer against fluctuations in electricity demand, usually peaks in the summer together with increased use of air conditioners.
Nuclear power plants and coal-fired power plants run at stable rates throughout the year regardless of fluctuations in power demand.
